Pacific Wrecks — B-17F-10-BO Flying Fortress 41-24521 «Black Jack»
Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress — the type: B-17F, four Wright R-1820 Cyclones, 22.7 m long, 31.6 m span

notes: Built by code (model_sources/L1_black_jack.py; tools/airkit.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. An own catalog entry (catalog/own_entries.json): the wreck has no Wikipedia article. The wreck sits upright on the sand, wheels up as she was ditched, settled a little into the bottom with a slight list: the nose badly crumpled and its glazing gone, the propellers of all four engines bent back, the turrets with their guns, the tail section a little twisted; a few panels beside her. Dressed with tools/dresskit.py: its own sediment (painted by Offlined with the seabed colour), the faded paint, the life of a warm-water wreck (soft corals, sponges, anemones, reef fish), textures and baked light. model_built.glb: the bomber as she flew in 1943, olive drab and neutral grey, the US star on the wings and the fuselage, the serial 124521 in yellow on the fin, standing on her wheels. Approximate: the heading and the exact position and depth (not published), the airframe (from the general drawings of the B-17F), the nose art (none is known, none is modelled).
